mx_meta_title: How binaural beats work, in plain words
mx_meta_desc: Binaural beats in plain words: one tone in each ear and the gap between them, what an EQ-SYNC session is like, and the 21 days session by session. Headphones needed.
mx_h1: How binaural beats work, without the jargon
mx_lead: One tone in each ear, through headphones, and the slow rhythm of the gap between them. That is the whole mechanism. Below: what it means, what a session is like and how the 21 days fall into place.
mx_line_h: How do binaural beats work, in one sentence?
mx_line_p1: Each ear receives a slightly different tone through headphones, and the brain rebuilds the gap between them as a slow rhythm.
mx_line_p2: A simple example, only to show the idea: a 200 Hz tone reaches the left ear and a 210 Hz tone reaches the right. Neither ear hears a rhythm. Yet you perceive a pulse ten times a second, as if a third sound existed. It is a teaching example, not an EQ-SYNC exercise.
mx_line_p3: That is why you need headphones. On speakers the two tones mix in the air before they reach your ears, and the binaural effect disappears. Use headphones with separate left and right sound, not a single earbud.
mx_entrain_h: What does it mean for brain activity to “synchronise” with a rhythm?
mx_entrain_p1: It is called brainwave entrainment. The idea: if you hear a slow, steady rhythm, the electrical activity of the brain might follow it. It is a hypothesis, not a certainty.
mx_entrain_p2: Researchers have not settled it. A 2023 systematic review found results pointing both ways: some studies support the idea, others contradict it. The science page shows exactly what the sources say.
mx_entrain_p3: We do not lean on this hypothesis as a promise. We use binaural sound as a frame: headphones, quiet, breathing, a daily appointment with yourself.
mx_bands_h: What are the delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma bands?
mx_bands_p1: They are slices of frequency into which the electrical activity of the brain is divided, as measured with an EEG. The limits differ a little from author to author. The ones below are those listed in a table of the 2023 review cited on the science page.
mx_bands_l1: Delta: 1–4 Hz. The slowest band, known from deep sleep.
mx_bands_l2: Theta: 5–8 Hz. Often seen on the way to sleep and in states of reverie.
mx_bands_l3: Alpha: 9–12 Hz. Typical of quiet wakefulness with the eyes closed.
mx_bands_l4: Beta: 13–30 Hz. Linked with active thinking and attention.
mx_bands_l5: Gamma: 32–48 Hz. The fastest of the five.
mx_session_h: What is an EQ-SYNC session like?
mx_session_p1: It is late evening. The house has gone quiet and your phone is on do not disturb. You sit down, put on your headphones and choose an exercise. The sound starts only when you press play, never on its own.
mx_session_p2: An exercise is guided: a voice leads you through breathing and relaxing the body while the binaural sound plays beneath it. There is nothing hard to do. You sit, you breathe, you listen.
mx_session_p3: At the end you take the headphones off and stay a minute in the quiet. There is no score and nothing to miss. If you want to hear how it sounds first, the sample is about 2 minutes long and sits on the home page.
mx_days_h: What do the 21 days look like, session by session?
mx_days_p1: The 21 days begin the moment you confirm your email address. The free programme has 4 guided exercises that you can repeat at any time within that window. We suggest one session a day, at a similar hour; the exact rhythm stays yours.
mx_days_l1: Day 1: you confirm your email and the count begins. You do the first session, no hurry.
mx_days_l2: Days 2–7: you get used to the ritual. The same hour, the same place, the same headphones.
mx_days_l3: Days 8–14: you return to the exercise you liked and try the others. They stay available for the whole window.
mx_days_l4: Days 15–19: the sessions become a habit. If you skipped a day, you simply carry on; the tracker adds up the days you listen.
mx_days_l5: Day 20: the bonus exercise “Relaxare profundă” unlocks, and it stays yours after the programme.
mx_days_l6: Day 21: the last day. Shortly before it you get a reminder email. After it, the 4 free exercises close and the bonus stays.
mx_why21_p1: Because a path needs a beginning and an end. Three weeks are enough to try the 4 exercises several times and see whether an evening ritual suits you.
mx_why21_p2: The number 21 is a choice of the programme, not a scientifically proven threshold. We do not claim there is a magic number after which something changes. We only say how long free access lasts and how it is counted: from the confirmation of your email.
mx_hear_h: What do you actually hear in an exercise?
mx_hear_p1: Two layers. The first is the binaural sound: the tones in each ear, discreet, heard as a warm background, sometimes with a faint pulse. The second is the voice, which leads you through breathing and relaxation.
mx_hear_p2: If you cannot hear the rhythm, that is not a problem. The binaural rhythm is a subtle perception and not everyone notices it. Focus on the voice and your breathing; with headphones on, the rest happens by itself.
mx_isnot_p1: It is not a treatment and it is not a medical device. It is a wellness tool: a sound frame for your evening. We promise no results and we do not replace medical or psychological care.
mx_isnot_p2: If you have epilepsy or a seizure disorder, do not use binaural audio without your doctor's agreement. The safety page says who should not listen and when to stop.
sc_meta_title: The science behind binaural sound, honestly
sc_meta_desc: What research does and does not show about binaural beats: three review papers, what each says, where they disagree, with the sources linked.
sc_h1: The science behind the sound: what research shows and does not show
sc_lead: The short answer: results are mixed. The phenomenon exists, but it is not settled whether, or how, the brain follows the rhythm. We read the sources as they are, not as we might wish.
sc_short_h: What does research show about binaural beats, in short?
sc_short_p1: A mixed picture. Some studies report effects on anxiety, mood or attention, and some find nothing or find effects in the opposite direction. The review papers say openly that the evidence is uneven.
sc_short_p2: We look here at three such papers: a 2023 systematic review and a 2015 literature review, both read at length, and a 2019 meta-analysis, read from its official abstract. Every claim below has a source.
sc_short_p3: EQ-SYNC is a wellness tool, not a treatment. We do not say the studies prove what our programme does; we say what researchers found and where it remains unclear.
sc_exists_p1: Yes, as a matter of perception. When two tones close in frequency are presented separately, one to each ear, the listener perceives an internal rhythm. The 2015 review (Chaieb and colleagues) notes, citing older work, that binaural beats were detected only when the carrier tone was below 1000 Hz.
sc_exists_p2: The 2023 review (Ingendoh and colleagues) says binaural beats can be perceived in the range of about 1–30 Hz. So the phenomenon itself is not in dispute; the debate begins at what it does to the brain.
sc_entrain_h: Does the brain synchronise its activity with a binaural rhythm?
sc_entrain_p1: It is not settled. Ingendoh and colleagues (PLOS ONE, 2023) reviewed fourteen published studies that measured brain activity. Five reported results in line with the brainwave entrainment hypothesis, eight reported contradictory results and one reported mixed results.
sc_entrain_p2: The authors explain why no firm conclusion can be drawn: the studies differ widely in frequencies, carrier tones, designs and measurements; most had no control group; samples were small (from 4 to 47 participants); and researchers do not even have a generally accepted definition of brainwave entrainment. Their conclusion calls for standardisation in future research.
sc_mood_h: What do studies say about anxiety, mood and attention?
sc_mood_p1: Chaieb and colleagues (Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2015) selected 30 papers. For cognition, results conflict from one study to the next. For mood, findings are mixed and point in different directions depending on the band used. For anxiety, several small studies, including patients before surgery and in emergency departments, reported lower anxiety compared with control sound.
sc_mood_p2: The 2019 meta-analysis (Garcia-Argibay, Santed and Reales, Psychological Research) pooled 22 studies. The authors conclude that exposure to binaural beats can affect cognition and can reduce anxiety and pain perception. They note that the effect depends on the frequency used, the time under exposure and the moment of exposure. For this paper we read the official abstract, not the full text.
sc_mood_p3: The two papers do not contradict each other head-on, but they do not say the same thing either: the first stresses how weak and inconsistent many effects are, the second an overall effect. Both rest on small studies done under different conditions.
sc_read_h: How do you read a news story about “brainwaves” and sound?
sc_read_p1: With three questions. How many people took part? Was there a control group, that is, a group that listened to an ordinary sound, and a fair comparison? Was brain activity measured (with an EEG) or only how people felt?
sc_read_p2: The 2023 review above shows why it matters: samples ranged from 4 to 47 participants, and most studies had no control group. When a headline promises a sure effect, find the study and see whether it answers these three questions.
sc_notshow_p1: The honest edge of today's knowledge, as the sources above describe it:
sc_notshow_l1: It does not show that binaural sound treats any condition. None of the cited papers claims that.
sc_notshow_l2: It does not show that everyone responds alike. The authors note that individual factors such as age or experience are not yet understood.
sc_notshow_l3: It does not show the ideal settings. Carrier frequency, beat frequency, session length and background noise remain unclear, says the 2015 review.
sc_notshow_l4: It does not show how the mechanism would work in the brain. The 2015 authors say the neural mechanisms are unclear.
sc_notshow_l5: It does not show whether any specific exercise, such as those in EQ-SYNC, has an effect. The studies concern the sounds each team used, not our programmes.
sc_ours_h: What does all this mean for EQ-SYNC?
sc_ours_p1: It means we invite you to a programme, not to a promise. We believe a quiet moment each evening, with headphones on and your breathing led by a voice, is worth something in itself. Binaural sound is our instrument, and research looks at it with interest and with reservations.
sc_ours_p2: If you want to see for yourself, you have 21 free days and a sample clip. If something does not suit you, you stop. And if you have health questions, they go to a doctor or a psychologist, not to a web page.
sc_sources_p1: All three are published scientific papers you can open:
sc_sources_l1: Ingendoh RM, Posny ES, Heine A. Binaural beats to entrain the brain? A systematic review of the effects of binaural beat stimulation on brain oscillatory activity. PLOS ONE, 2023.
sc_sources_l2: Chaieb L, Wilpert EC, Reber TP, Fell J. Auditory beat stimulation and its effects on cognition and mood states. Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2015.
sc_sources_l3: Garcia-Argibay M, Santed MA, Reales JM. Efficacy of binaural auditory beats in cognition, anxiety, and pain perception: a meta-analysis. Psychological Research, 2019 (PubMed abstract).
ls_meta_title: How to listen: headphones, volume, time and posture
ls_meta_desc: How to listen to binaural audio: which headphones, how quietly, at what time, in what posture and when to stop. A practical guide for your evening.
ls_h1: How to listen properly: headphones, volume, time and posture
ls_lead: A few small choices separate a calm session from one spent fighting the sound. Put your headphones on, turn the volume down and let the evening slow.
ls_headphones_p1: Any stereo headphones with separate left and right sound. Over-ear ones are the most comfortable if you lie down; earbuds work too if they sit well and do not press. Wired or wireless makes no difference as long as both channels are active.
ls_headphones_p2: A single earbud will not do, and neither will the phone speaker. The binaural effect depends on the different tone each ear receives. Also check your phone settings: if “mono audio” is switched on (under accessibility), switch it off, or the two channels will blend.
ls_volume_h: How loud should the volume be?
ls_volume_p1: Quieter than you would think. Set a level at which the voice is clear but does not press on you. The binaural sound should not fill the room; it sits under the voice, like a background.
ls_volume_p2: Protect your hearing. The World Health Organization, together with ITU, published a standard for personal audio devices built on a “sound allowance”; for adults the reference mode is 80 dB for 40 hours a week. A calm exercise, listened to quietly, stays well under that.
ls_volume_p3: If your ears ring or sound feels muffled after a session, the volume was too high. Turn it down next time.
ls_time_h: What time of day is best for listening?
ls_time_p1: The hour at which you can afford to slow down. For many that means evening, a little before sleep, after the screens have gone off. For others it is an afternoon pause. There is no magic hour.
ls_time_p2: It matters more to choose an hour and keep it. The same hour each day turns the session into a ritual the body recognises. If you fall asleep during a session, that is fine; take the headphones off when you wake.
ls_posture_h: In what position should you listen?
ls_posture_p1: One in which you can stay still without effort: lying on your back with a pillow under your knees, or sitting in an armchair with your back supported. Leave your hands loose, perhaps one on your chest or belly so you can feel your breathing.
ls_posture_p2: Close your eyes or let your gaze go soft. Put your phone on do not disturb. For as long as the session lasts, there is nothing else to do.
ls_posture_p3: Never listen while driving, cycling, crossing the street or operating machinery. Binaural sound asks for quiet, not divided attention.
ls_routine_h: How do you make this a 21-day routine?
ls_routine_p1: Start small. One session a day, at the same hour, in the same place. Set things up beforehand: charged headphones, a blanket, a glass of water.
ls_routine_p2: Do not scold yourself if you skipped a day. The programme does not count missed days, only added ones, and your 21 days stay yours. Pick up from where you are. The day-by-day details are on the method page.
ls_nothing_p1: That is fine. Not every listener notices the binaural rhythm, and there is no “you should feel”. Research itself is mixed; see the science page.
ls_nothing_p2: Put less weight on the sound and more on the ritual: the same hour, headphones on, the slow breathing of the voice. If after a few sessions it does not feel right, do not carry on out of duty. The programme is free and you can stop at any time.
ls_annoying_h: What if the sound bothers you?
ls_annoying_p1: Turn the volume down. If it still bothers you, stop the session. A continuous sound with a faint pulse can be unpleasant for some, especially when tired.
ls_annoying_p2: You can try other headphones, another time of day or a day's break. If the discomfort returns, do not force it. EQ-SYNC is not for everyone and does not have to be.
ls_evening_h: What does a listening evening look like, step by step?
ls_evening_p1: A simple order you can adjust:
ls_evening_l1: Finish what can be finished and put your phone on do not disturb.
ls_evening_l2: Charge your headphones and choose the place: bed, armchair, sofa.
ls_evening_l3: Switch off the main light; leave a warm one if you like.
ls_evening_l4: Put the headphones on, set the volume low and press play.
ls_evening_l5: Follow the voice. If your mind runs off, come back to your breathing, without scolding yourself.
ls_evening_l6: At the end, take the headphones off and stay a minute in the quiet.
ls_stop_p1: Stop and take the headphones off if you feel dizzy, get a headache, feel discomfort, or if restlessness grows instead of fading. It is not a failure, it is information.
ls_stop_p2: If you have epilepsy or a seizure disorder, do not use binaural audio without your doctor's agreement. If you have other health or hearing problems, talk to your doctor first.
ls_stop_p3: If you or someone close to you is in immediate danger, call 112.
gl_meta_title: Glossary: binaural, alpha, theta, delta, isochronic
gl_meta_desc: The EQ-SYNC glossary: binaural beats, carrier tone, beat frequency, brainwave entrainment, isochronic tones and the delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma bands, defined simply.
gl_h1: Glossary: the words around binaural sound
gl_lead: The terms you will meet on the site and in research, defined briefly and without jargon. Where a term has uncertain limits, we say so.
gl_binaural_p1: An auditory illusion: when the left and right ears receive, through headphones, two tones close in frequency, the brain perceives a rhythm equal to the difference between them. The rhythm does not exist in the air; it forms in the listener.
gl_binaural_p2: A teaching example: 200 Hz in one ear and 210 Hz in the other give a perceived pulse ten times a second. Headphones are needed.
gl_carrier_p1: The base tone, the one you actually hear, in each ear. The difference between the two carrier tones is the binaural rhythm. A 2015 review notes that binaural beats were detected only with carriers below 1000 Hz.
gl_beatfreq_p1: The number of pulses per second, measured in hertz (Hz), equal to the difference between the two tones. A 2023 review says binaural beats can be perceived in the range of about 1–30 Hz.
gl_hz_p1: A unit of frequency: how many cycles happen in one second. 10 Hz means ten cycles a second. The lower the number, the slower the rhythm.
gl_monaural_p1: Physical beats: two close tones are summed before they reach the ears, and the result is a sound whose volume pulses. They exist in the air, unlike binaural beats. That is why they can be heard without headphones.
gl_isochronic_p1: A single tone switched on and off at equal intervals, like a regular pulse. The rhythm is in the sound itself and does not form in the brain as it does with binaural beats, so they do not necessarily need headphones. They are a category apart from binaural beats.
gl_isochronic_p2: EQ-SYNC works with binaural beats; that is why we ask you to use headphones.
gl_entrainment_p1: The hypothesis that the electrical activity of the brain might oscillate at the same frequency as an external rhythmic stimulus. The 2023 review notes that there is no generally accepted definition and that study results point both ways.
gl_entrainment_p2: It is a research hypothesis, not a promise of our programme. Details on the science page.
gl_eeg_p1: The electroencephalogram: a way of measuring, with electrodes on the scalp, the electrical activity of the brain. Research on brainwave entrainment uses it to see whether activity follows the rhythm heard.
gl_bands_h: What are the brain's frequency bands?
gl_bands_p1: Slices of frequency into which activity measured with an EEG is divided: delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma. Limits differ slightly between authors. The ones below come from a table of a 2023 review.
gl_delta_p1: The slowest band, 1–4 Hz. We know it from deep sleep.
gl_theta_p1: The 5–8 Hz band. Often seen on the way to sleep and in states of reverie, when the mind wanders.
gl_alpha_p1: The 9–12 Hz band. Typical of quiet wakefulness with the eyes closed, like the start of a calm evening.
gl_beta_p1: The 13–30 Hz band, linked with active thinking and attention.
gl_gamma_p1: The fastest of the five, 32–48 Hz in the table cited.
gl_control_p1: A group of participants given a comparison condition, for example an ordinary sound instead of the one being tested. Without it, you cannot know whether a change comes from the tested sound or from something else, such as people simply sitting quietly for a few minutes.
gl_placebo_p1: The change someone feels because they expect it or because they are given attention, not because the intervention has an effect of its own. That is why good studies compare with a control group.
gl_systematic_p1: A review that searches for all studies on a topic by rules set in advance and describes them together. The 2023 review of binaural beats is of this kind.
gl_metaanalysis_p1: An analysis that statistically combines the results of several studies into one result. The 2019 meta-analysis of binaural beats pooled 22 studies.
gl_session_h: What do session, exercise and protocol mean at EQ-SYNC?
gl_session_p1: An exercise is a guided recording built on binaural beats. A session is your moment of listening. A protocol is a set of 4 exercises on one theme, grouped in one of the 10 categories. The free 21-day programme has 4 exercises and a bonus on day 20.
gl_wellness_h: What does “wellness tool, not a medical device” mean?
gl_wellness_p1: It means EQ-SYNC is made for wellbeing and calm, not for diagnosis or treatment. It does not replace medical or psychological care and promises no cures.
wh_meta_title: Who EQ-SYNC is for: evenings, focus, stress
wh_meta_desc: Who EQ-SYNC is for: a quiet end to the evening, a pause before work, a heavy stretch. Who should not listen. It is not a treatment.
wh_lead: For adults who want a quiet, sound-guided moment at the end of a full day. Not for treatment, not for diagnosis.
wh_intro_p1: For adults, 18 and over, whose minds stay “on the run” long after the day has ended. If you recognise evenings when your thoughts will not stop, EQ-SYNC offers a 21-day path, session by session, with headphones on.
wh_intro_p2: It also suits the sceptical. We do not ask you to believe anything: you listen to a clip of a couple of minutes, read what research says and decide for yourself.
wh_evening_h: Can I use it to wind down in the evening?
wh_evening_p1: Yes, this is the main case. It is 9:40 p.m., you have finished everything that could be finished, and your mind is still counting what is left. A session settles you into a simple ritual: headphones, a voice, breathing, a few minutes only for you.
wh_evening_p2: We do not promise sleep. We offer an evening that slows down, something for the body to hold on to. Details on hour and posture are on the how to listen page.
wh_focus_h: Can I use EQ-SYNC before a task that needs attention?
wh_focus_p1: You can, as a transition pause: a few minutes of guided breathing before you start work. Some protocol categories are called “Claritate mentală și decizii” or “Performanță cognitivă și concentrare”.
wh_focus_p2: Be wary of promises, ours included: we do not say you will focus better. We say we offer a structured moment of quiet beforehand. Research on attention and binaural sound is mixed, as the science page shows.
wh_stress_h: And in a heavy, stressful stretch?
wh_stress_p1: A guided breathing exercise at the end of the day can be a pause. That is all. We do not diagnose your state and we do not treat it.
wh_stress_p2: If the stress lasts, or if it affects your sleep or daily life, talk to a psychologist or your doctor. EQ-SYNC is made by the same team that runs Psizone, the psychology centre in Galați, where you can ask for an assessment.
wh_ask_h: What to ask of EQ-SYNC, and what not to ask?
wh_ask_l1: Ask it for a ritual: a fixed hour, headphones, a voice, slow breathing.
wh_ask_l2: Ask it for a structured pause between day and evening.
wh_ask_l3: Do not ask it for a diagnosis, a treatment or a fix for a health problem.
wh_ask_l4: Do not ask it to replace a psychologist, a psychotherapist or a doctor.
wh_ask_l5: Do not ask it for a sure result. We do not promise one.
wh_sleep_h: But what if my sleep is poor?
wh_sleep_p1: EQ-SYNC can be an evening ritual before sleep, and that is all. It is not a treatment for insomnia and we do not promise you will sleep better.
wh_sleep_p2: If light sleep or tired wake-ups have lasted for weeks, tell a doctor or a psychologist. It may be something a sound cannot solve.
wh_not_p1: There are situations in which it is not suitable:
wh_not_l1: People under 18. The programme is for those who have turned 18.
wh_not_l2: People with epilepsy or seizure disorders, without their doctor's agreement.
wh_not_l3: Anyone seeking a diagnosis or a treatment. EQ-SYNC is a wellness tool, not a medical device.
wh_not_l4: Anyone who is driving, cycling or operating a machine. Listen only when safe, seated or lying down.
wh_not_l5: Anyone who feels in danger. If you or someone close to you is in immediate danger, call 112.
wh_start_p1: You have 21 free days from confirming your email. Take your headphones, pick an evening and start the first session. No strings attached.
sf_meta_title: Safety: who should not use binaural audio
sf_meta_desc: EQ-SYNC safety: a wellness tool, not a medical device. Epilepsy and seizure disorders, age, hearing, when to stop, and the 112 number.
sf_lead: A wellness tool, not a medical device. Not for people with epilepsy or seizure disorders without their doctor's agreement.
sf_status_h: Is EQ-SYNC a medical device or a treatment?
sf_status_p1: No. EQ-SYNC is a wellness tool, not a medical device, and it does not replace medical consultation or treatment. We do not diagnose, we do not treat and we promise no results.
sf_status_p2: If you have a health problem, the first step is your doctor or a psychologist. This page says what we know about listening safely, not what a sound can treat.
sf_epilepsy_h: Who should not listen to binaural audio?
sf_epilepsy_p1: People with epilepsy or seizure disorders do not use binaural audio without their doctor's agreement. Tell your doctor what you plan to listen to and ask for an opinion before the first session.
sf_epilepsy_p2: This is a precaution, not a finding of a study: we did not find a source that quantifies the risk, so we choose to be cautious. If you doubt whether you have such a condition, treat that as a reason to talk to a doctor first.
sf_health_h: What if you have other health problems or take medication?
sf_health_p1: Talk to your doctor before you begin. A sound is no reason to change or stop any medication, and we give no advice about medication. Those are discussed with your doctor or psychiatrist.
sf_health_p2: The same applies if you have hearing problems, ringing in the ears or recent ear surgery: ask your doctor first.
sf_pregnancy_h: Can I use EQ-SYNC if I am pregnant?
sf_pregnancy_p1: We have no recommendation for or against this case. As with any new routine in pregnancy, ask the doctor who follows you first.
sf_age_p1: Yes. The programme is for people who have turned 18.
sf_hearing_h: How do you protect your hearing?
sf_hearing_p1: Listen quietly, with headphones that sit well. If after a session you feel ringing or the sound seems muffled, the volume was too high. Details on the how to listen page, including what the WHO–ITU standard says for personal audio devices.
sf_stop_p1: Stop and take the headphones off if you feel dizzy, get a headache, feel discomfort or if restlessness grows. Never listen while driving, cycling or operating a machine.
sf_crisis_h: What if you are in danger?
sf_crisis_p1: If you or someone close to you is in immediate danger, call 112. EQ-SYNC is not an emergency service and cannot respond to a crisis.
ab_meta_title: About EQ-SYNC: the team and company in Galați
ab_meta_desc: Who makes EQ-SYNC: founder Adrian Turcu, the company EQSYNC SRL in Galați, the link with Psizone and how we work. A wellness tool, not a treatment.
ab_what_p1: A 21-day programme of guided listening, built on binaural beats, for mental calm. You listen with headphones, evening after evening, at your own pace. The first 21 days are free.
ab_what_p2: It is a wellness tool. It is not a treatment and not a medical device.
ab_who_p1: EQ-SYNC was created by Adrian Turcu, a psychologist, educational psychologist and couple and family psychotherapist with more than 20 years of clinical experience. The company is EQSYNC SRL in Galați, and the programme is made by the same team that runs Psizone, the psychology centre in Galați.
ab_who_p2: We are real people and a real company, with public registration details shown in the footer of every page.
ab_how_h: How do we write, and what do we promise?
ab_how_p1: We write plainly, with true numbers: 21 days, 4 exercises, one session a day. We give no percentages and promise no cures. When we talk about research, we name the source; see the science page.
ab_how_p2: Pages that touch on health are marked as such and are published after review by a named specialist. The EQ-SYNC guide answers only from reviewed content.
ab_estate_h: How is EQ-SYNC linked to Psizone and Hemi-Sync România?
ab_estate_p1: Psizone is the neuropsychology centre in Galați where EQ-SYNC was born; that is where you go for clinical questions. Hemi-Sync România offers the Monroe Institute® programmes in Romanian. They are different sites with different audiences and rules, and EQ-SYNC remains a separate wellness tool.
ab_contact_p1: The contact page has the company details. For clinical questions beyond the programme, you can reach us through Psizone.
pr_meta_desc: The 10 EQ-SYNC protocol categories, 4 protocols each, how to choose, how the subscription works and the 14-day withdrawal right. Listening with headphones.
pr_what_p1: A set of 4 guided exercises on one theme. Protocols are grouped in 10 categories, 4 in each, so 40 in all. You listen with headphones, just like the exercises of the free programme.
pr_what_p2: They are for after the 21 days, if you want to continue. They are not compulsory and they are not a treatment.
pr_choose_h: How do you choose a category?
pr_choose_p1: Start from your moment and your theme. If the evening is the hard part, look at “Calmare, stres și reglare” or “Somn și regenerare”. If you need a start to the day, there is “Dimineață, energie și activare”. For desk work, “Claritate mentală și decizii” or “Performanță cognitivă și concentrare”.
pr_choose_p2: You do not choose for an illness, but for a moment. And if you do not know, begin with the free 21-day programme and see what suits you.
pr_after_h: How do you reach a protocol after the free programme?
pr_after_p1: The 4 free exercises close after day 21, and you get an email before that. The bonus exercise “Relaxare profundă”, unlocked on day 20, stays yours. If you want to continue, you choose a protocol.

fx_meta_title: Questions about binaural beats and EQ-SYNC
fx_meta_desc: 25 answers about EQ-SYNC: the 21-day programme, headphones and listening, what science says about binaural beats, safety, protocols and withdrawal.
fx_h1: Questions about binaural beats and EQ-SYNC
fx_lead: Short answers in one place: the programme, headphones, research, safety and protocols. If you cannot find what you need, ask the guide.
fx_program_1_a: The moment you confirm your email address. From then you have 21 days to work through the free programme at your own pace.
fx_program_2_a: You put on your headphones, choose a quiet place and an exercise, and press play. A voice guides you through breathing and relaxation while the binaural sound plays beneath it. Sound never starts on its own.
fx_program_3_a: Yes. The first 21 days are on us, with no strings attached. The programme has 4 guided exercises, and on day 20 a bonus exercise unlocks.
fx_program_4_a: The 4 free exercises close after day 21, and you get an email before that. The bonus exercise “Relaxare profundă” stays yours. If you want to continue, you can choose protocols.
fx_program_5_a: Yes. You can repeat any of the 4 exercises at any time within the 21 days. There are no missed days, only added ones.
fx_program_6_a: Because a path needs a beginning and an end, and three weeks are enough to try the 4 exercises several times. The number is a choice of the programme, not a scientifically proven threshold.
fx_program_7_a: Yes. The programme is for people who have turned 18.
fx_casti_1_a: Yes, always. The binaural effect depends on the different tone each ear receives, and speakers blend the tones before they reach your ears. Use stereo headphones with separate left and right sound.
fx_casti_2_a: Any stereo headphones that sit well: over-ear or earbuds, wired or wireless. A single earbud will not do. If your phone has “mono audio” switched on under accessibility, switch it off.
fx_casti_3_a: Quietly, at a level where the voice is clear and does not press on you. If your ears ring or sound feels muffled after a session, turn the volume down next time.
fx_casti_4_q: What time is best to listen?
fx_casti_4_a: The hour at which you can slow down: for many, in the evening a little before sleep; for others, an afternoon pause. Keeping the hour matters more than which hour it is.
fx_casti_5_q: Can I fall asleep during a session?
fx_casti_5_a: You can, that is fine. Take the headphones off when you wake. If yours are uncomfortable lying down, choose soft over-ear ones.
fx_casti_6_q: Can I listen while driving or working?
fx_casti_6_a: No. Listen only when safe, seated or lying down. Do not listen at the wheel, on a bike, in the street or operating a machine.
fx_stiinta_1_a: A perceptual phenomenon: each ear receives, through headphones, a slightly different tone, and the brain perceives the difference as a slow rhythm. The rhythm does not exist in the air; it forms in the listener.
fx_stiinta_2_a: Research is mixed. Some studies report effects on anxiety or attention, others find nothing, and a 2023 review found results in both directions. We promise no results; the science page shows the sources.
fx_stiinta_3_q: What are alpha, theta and delta waves?
fx_stiinta_3_a: They are frequency bands of the brain's electrical activity, measured with an EEG: delta 1–4 Hz, theta 5–8 Hz, alpha 9–12 Hz (per a table in a 2023 review). Limits vary slightly between authors. You will find them in the glossary.
fx_stiinta_4_a: That is fine: not every listener notices the binaural rhythm. Put the weight on the ritual, that is, the same hour, headphones and slow breathing, and if it does not suit you, you can stop at any time.
fx_stiinta_5_q: What is the difference between binaural and isochronic?
fx_stiinta_5_a: With binaural beats the rhythm forms in the brain from two different tones, one in each ear, so you need headphones. With isochronic tones a single tone is switched on and off regularly, so the rhythm is in the sound. EQ-SYNC uses binaural beats.
fx_siguranta_1_q: Is it a medical device or a treatment?
fx_siguranta_1_a: No. EQ-SYNC is a wellness tool, not a medical device, and it does not replace medical consultation or treatment.
fx_siguranta_2_a: Yes. People with epilepsy or seizure disorders do not use binaural audio without their doctor's agreement. More on the safety page.
fx_siguranta_3_q: Can I use EQ-SYNC if I take medication or have a condition?
fx_siguranta_3_a: Talk to your doctor first. We give no advice about medication, and a sound is no reason to change or stop any treatment.
fx_siguranta_4_q: What do I do if I feel unwell while listening?
fx_siguranta_4_a: Stop and take the headphones off. If dizziness, a headache or discomfort persists, talk to a doctor. If you or someone close to you is in immediate danger, call 112.
fx_protocoale_1_a: A set of 4 guided exercises on one theme. Protocols are grouped in 10 categories, and you choose them, if you wish, after the 21 free days.
fx_protocoale_2_a: Yes. Each protocol takes one place in the subscription and you can swap it from one month to the next.
fx_protocoale_3_q: What if I am not happy with a protocol I bought?
fx_protocoale_3_a: You have 14 days from purchase in which to withdraw from the contract for that protocol and get your money back, even if you have listened to it. Monthly renewals are not refunded. Details are on the right of withdrawal page.
